summary: Iteration 3 backend + frontend testing for Beet.Health CRM (reminders, custom fields, clickable metrics, tracker import). Extended /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py from 30 -> 42 tests covering all new endpoints. Result: 42/42 pytest PASSED. Frontend: verified admin dashboard clickable tiles (stat-conversions -> /all-leads?status=Converted; stat-overdue -> /all-leads?follow_up=overdue), Settings tabs (settings-tab-custom adds a dropdown custom field, settings-tab-import parses CSV and shows import-summary), send-reminders-btn works for admin and is hidden for Harry (employee). New Lead dialog renders the custom-field-* inputs including the newly created field. All flows functional; the earlier iteration_2 owner-reassignment fix now passes (cascade of followup_assigned_to on owner change).

minor.issue: 5/10min per-email rate limit still active; test suite pre-clears otps collection via pymongo to avoid 429 during parallel runs.
Runs synchronously and iterates all active users -> could be slow with large teams; consider a background task / batching.
Duplicate check inside loop uses find_one per row (N queries); acceptable for spec limit of 2000 rows but could be bulk-normalized. Also does not stream a progress signal.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1104 lines — over the 700-line guideline. Split into modules: auth.py, leads.py, options_and_cf.py, imports.py, reminders.py, tasks_and_activities.py.
import_commit performs a Mongo find_one per row inside a for loop; batch pre-fetch of existing normalized_phone/normalized_email would be more efficient for large trackers.

reminder_scheduler() uses raw asyncio loop; if backend restarts twice a minute during dev it can double-fire on the same day. Adding a last_reminder timestamp guard would be safer (already tracked in db.system).
CustomFieldIn.type is a free-form string — should be validated against the fixed TYPES enum to prevent bad data.

list_leads filter for follow_up=upcoming does not respect status closed exclusion; overdue also does not exclude closed statuses — could inflate 'overdue follow-ups' tile counts by counting closed leads with a stale next_follow_up. build_user_followups() correctly excludes closed statuses but the /api/leads?follow_up=overdue filter does not.
test_credentials: OTP dev-mode; POST /api/auth/request-otp returns dev_otp. Seeded: admin@beet.health, manager@beet.health, harry/leo/ben/emma@beet.health.
seed_data_creation: None persistent; all TEST_-prefixed leads / custom fields / options / tasks are cleaned up in-test. TEST_UI_* rows created during Playwright run were removed via mongo cleanup.
context_for_next_testing_agent: backend_test.py now covers reminders, custom fields, follow_up filter, and tracker import in addition to iteration_1/2 flows. Run with `pytest -n 0` to avoid OTP rate-limit collisions (pytest.ini defaults to -n 2 loadscope which mostly works because fixtures re-clear otps per email). For the file-upload Playwright step, note that the import-file-input is intentionally hidden; use `page.locator(...).set_input_files(...)` and avoid wait_for_selector visible on it.
rca of the issue: No new blocker bugs. Only note: /api/leads?follow_up=overdue does not filter out closed statuses, so it can differ slightly from the personalized reminders view. Not a spec violation for this iteration but flagged for review.
